newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA FACES DIFFICULTIES SERVICING DOMESTIC DEBT.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA FACES DIFFICULTIES SERVICING DOMESTIC DEBT.

text.p: Bulgaria's Finance Ministry is expected cover maturity payments on government securities due this week with new issues of treasury paper in a bid to meet skyrocketing domestic debt payments, an official said on Monday.
"Maturity payments on treasury paper due this week exceed 24 billion levs. Most of it will be covered by offering special issues of treasury paper," a finance ministry official told Reuters.
The official, who declined to be named, rejected local media speculations that the government is about to declare a moratorium on domestic debt payments.
"We have not yet used up all available instruments," said the official.
Three-year T-notes with par value of 500 million levs mature on September 2. September 3 is the maturity date of another issue, 18-month T-notes worth of 823 million levs.
On September 4 the ministry is due to pay principal and interest on three T-bill issues with total par value of around 23.2 billion levs, Finance Ministry figures show.
Record high interest rate of 108 percent has stretched the budget deficit as maturity payments now exceed net sales of government securities, analysts said.
The ministry has so far received 5.4 billion levs from a 49-day discount and six-month floated coupon T-bills auctioned on Friday.
The ministry placed a further four billion levs worth of three-month discount T-bills at today's auction, results of which will be available on Tuesday.

In a move to raise more cash for maturity payments the ministry is now negotiating with local commercial banks, the United Bulgarian Bank being one of them, for selling to it around 1.5 billion levs of treasury paper, said the official.
The State Savings Bank will be offered a similar deal.
Under the Bulgarian National Bank Act the finance ministry is entitled to a three-month credit from the BNB, which should not exceed five percent of the annual state budget revenue.
This year's credit amounts to around 6.5 billion levs, the official said.

In a bid to prevent increase of money supply, last week the BNB and the finance ministry urged bank managers and dealers of treasury paper invest funds released by paper maturities in the new issues of government securities.
